TNA/TNI EngineTraining needs analysis software, backed by evidence.

Edstellar's TNA/TNI Engine runs your complete training needs analysis and training needs identification cycle, from raw employee data to a validated, prioritized training roadmap and calendar.

  • Self, manager, assessment, interview and focus-group evidence behind every need
  • Needs ranked by gap, criticality and headcount
  • A TNA report, roadmap, calendar and IDPs at the end of one cycle

Training needs confirmed by five sources of evidence.

A training need never rests on one opinion. Ratings, assessments, interviews and focus groups are combined, and every need is tested before it reaches the plan.

Source 02 · AnchorIn view

Manager rating anchors the gap

Self minus manager is the perception gap. With no manager rating, the self rating is used and the need is flagged low-confidence.

101 · Rater

Each direct report, one by one

Team assessments use the same instrument as the self-rating.

202 · Scale

1 to 4 in half steps

Awareness, Working, Practitioner, Expert. 2.5 reads as Working+.

303 · Unbiased

Target level stays hidden

Raters never see the level the role needs, and no answer is pre-selected.

Five sources · statusInterviews and focus groups attach to a cohort, never to one person

  1. 01Individual

    Self-rating

    Employees rate their own proficiency on every skill their role needs.

  2. 02In view · anchor

    Manager rating

    Managers rate each direct report on the same items.

  3. 03Imported

    Assessments

    Skills and talent results, an objective measure alongside ratings.

  4. 04Cohort level

    Interviews

    Role holders and leaders explain the context and causes behind gaps.

  5. 05Cohort level

    Focus groups

    Cross-functional groups of 8 to 10 test what the survey found.

Verdict legendConfirmed by a facilitator

CorroboratesConfidence rises; the need goes ahead with evidence attached.

ContradictsProcess, tooling or staffing; routed as a non-training intervention.

ExtendsA net-new need; enters through a governed framework amendment.

Interview and focus-group findings attach to a cohort (role, department, level), never to what one person said.

One TNA/TNI cycle, from raw data to a training calendar.

Fifteen stages in five phases. Each phase hands a finished, approved output to the next, so the analysis never runs on unvalidated data.

Phase1 of 5

01
Set up

See all 15 stages and quality gates

Phase 01 · Stages 1 to 4

Set up

Configure the organization with a guided wizard, import and clean the employee data, and build the competency framework the whole cycle measures against.

  1. 01Organization setup
  2. 02Data import and cleanup
  3. 03Competency framework
  4. 04Framework sign-off and lock

GateThe HR Head signs off and locks the framework.

Hands overA clean employee master and a locked, versioned framework

Phase 02 · Stages 5 to 7

Assess

The survey builds itself from the locked framework, so each person rates only the skills their role needs. Managers rate their direct reports, and assessment results are imported alongside.

  1. 05Survey build
  2. 06Self, manager and assessment ratings
  3. 07Survey analysis

GateThe survey deploys only on a locked framework with an open window.

Hands overA skills matrix and the gaps to probe

Phase 03 · Stages 8 and 9

Validate

Department Heads review flagged ratings and calibrate with an attributed reason. Interviews and focus groups then test the gaps the survey surfaced.

  1. 08Rating calibration
  2. 09Interviews and focus groups

No hold-upsCalibration is exception-based, so it never blocks the cycle.

Hands overCalibrated ratings and themes tied to the findings they test

Phase 04 · Stages 10 to 12

Analyze

Every source is reconciled into one need set per person. Gaps are scored by severity and criticality, prioritized, and written up in a composable TNA report.

  1. 10Consolidation
  2. 11Gap analysis
  3. 12TNA report

GateThe HR Head approves and locks the TNA report.

Hands overAn approved TNA report with prioritized needs

Phase 05 · Stages 13 to 15

Plan

Needs are grouped into programs, with non-training causes routed to the right owner. Development plans and learning paths follow, then a quarterly roadmap and a training calendar.

  1. 13TNI and non-training interventions
  2. 14Development plans and learning paths
  3. 15Roadmap, budget and training calendar

GateThe HR Head approves and locks the roadmap, then the calendar.

Hands overA locked roadmap, calendar, IDPs and learning paths

Every AI draft is reviewed by your team.

The TNA/TNI Engine uses AI to draft the slow parts of a cycle. A person reviews every draft and chooses one of three actions: Accept, Modify or Manual. Try the controls: switch a step off or change the deployment mode.

AI-assisted stepsSample data

  1. 01Step 1 of 9: Setup field suggestions. Default action set by Program Admin.Manual
  2. 02Step 2 of 9: Job description parsing. Default action set by Program Admin.Manual
  3. 03Step 3 of 9: Skill matching and framework alignment. Default action: Accept suggested, high confidence.AcceptManual
  4. 04Step 4 of 9: Note extraction. Default action set by Program Admin.Manual
  5. 05Step 5 of 9: Theme synthesis. Default action: Always modify, medium confidence.ModifyManual
  6. 06Step 6 of 9: Non-training classification and deduplication. Default action set by Program Admin.Manual
  7. 07Step 7 of 9: Learning-path generation. Default action: Always modify, medium confidence.ModifyManual
  8. 08Step 8 of 9: Report narrative. Default action: Always modify, medium confidence.ModifyManual
  9. 09Step 9 of 9: Service recommendations. Default action set by Program Admin.Manual

Acceptkept as draftedModifyedited firstManualdone by hand

Deployment modeSet once per cycle

The model runs inside your own cloud tenancy, so your data never leaves it.

  • Program Admin sets the mode and every step. HR Head can view.
  • After the survey is deployed, a mode change needs HR Head approval. Every change is logged.
